notes: HOW FACTS WERE CHECKED. Every headcount in this file was read on the page it cites (fetched and searched for the figure). The web-search allowance ran out part-way through, so many plants have no headcount: they are null, not estimated. Existence and addresses of plants without a company page among their sources come from the EPA Toxics Release Inventory facility list for Texas (the URL in their sources), where each is listed as not closed, together with the researcher's general knowledge of the industry; they were not each re-confirmed on a 2026 company page. Product lines and opening years without a cited page are general knowledge and worth a second look. COORDINATES. Exact house-number matches from the geocoder were used where it gave one. Where it matched only the street, the EPA list's coordinate was used when it agreed with the street and with the known layout: Dow Freeport, Dow Deer Park, Dow Texas City, LyondellBasell La Porte and Houston Refinery, BASF Port Arthur, INEOS Chocolate Bayou, Battleground, Texas City and Green Lake, OxyChem La Porte, Pasadena and Battleground, Westlake Epoxy, Ketjen Bayport and Pasadena, Ascend, Indorama, Arkema Clear Lake, Chemours Corpus Christi, Shintech, Valero Port Arthur and Three Rivers, Phillips 66 Sweeny, CITGO, both Flint Hills plants, TotalEnergies La Porte, Delek Big Spring, Air Liquide Bayport, Linde Texas City. EPA coordinates are rounded to seconds and some are inside the fence rather than at the gate. Street-level points (on the right road beside the plant, not a house number) were accepted for: Gulf Coast Growth Ventures (FM 2986), LyondellBasell Corpus Christi (McKinzie Rd), Westlake Longview (Estes Dr), Celanese Bishop (County Road 4), and the Phillips 66 and Chevron Phillips plants at Borger (both on Spur 119, given the same point). These are the first to re-check. Wikipedia coordinates were used for ExxonMobil Baytown, Pemex Deer Park and Valero McKee. Olin Freeport is inside the Dow complex and shares its point; INVISTA Victoria and LyondellBasell Victoria are neighbours on one site and geocode to almost the same point. HEADCOUNT CAVEATS. ExxonMobil Baytown (7,000) is Harris County's figure and almost certainly counts contractors. Figures taken from undated pages (Valero and Phillips 66 refinery pages, the Victoria and Brazosport lists, the BASF Texas total) carry 2026, the year they were read. LyondellBasell's fact sheets say "Total Employees" without saying whether contractors are in. The Chevron Phillips Sweeny and OxyChem Texas figures include contractors by the companies' own wording. FIGURES SEEN ONLY IN SEARCH SUMMARIES AND LEFT OUT (the company sites refused automated requests or the page could not be opened): ExxonMobil's 2026 Baytown fact sheet, about 1,900 employees and 4,800 contract personnel (corporate.exxonmobil.com); Dow's Texas flyer, 2022: Freeport 3,666 employees and 2,450 contractors, Seadrift 726 and 563, Texas 7,198 employees (corporate.dow.com/content/dam/corp/documents/location/dow-in-texas-flyer.pdf); Dow Deer Park "nearly 700" and Texas City 330 (corporate.dow.com location pages); Eastman Longview "over 1,500"; Marathon Galveston Bay 1,550 and Motiva Port Arthur 1,450 (Wikipedia infoboxes, undated); TotalEnergies Port Arthur about 650; CITGO Corpus Christi "more than 1,000 jobs locally" (a 2017 company release that does not separate contractors). A reviewer with a browser can confirm these quickly. JUDGMENT CALLS. ExxonMobil's Baytown refinery, chemical plant and olefins plant are one plant; Beaumont refinery, chemical and lubricants are one plant with the polyethylene plant on Highway 90 kept apart. Valero's two Corpus Christi refineries are one plant because the company reports them together; Flint Hills' two are kept apart. BASF TotalEnergies Petrochemicals is listed as a BASF plant (60% owner and operator). Pemex Deer Park is its own company with parent Pemex; Shell keeps the chemical plant on the same site. OxyChem's parent is given as Berkshire Hathaway on the strength of reports that the purchase closed on 2 January 2026 (not opened on a primary page). Covestro's parent is given as XRG (ADNOC) from the Baytown foundation's report. Goodyear agreed in 2025 to sell its chemical business, which includes the Beaumont and Houston plants; whether the sale closed and what the business is now called could not be checked, so the plants are still listed under Goodyear. CITGO's ownership was the subject of a court-ordered sale and its parent is left null. LyondellBasell's Houston Refinery is listed as closed (refining ended in 2025). LEFT OUT FOR LACK OF A CHECKED SOURCE OR ADDRESS: AbbVie (Allergan) Waco, Fujifilm Biotechnologies College Station, Lonza Houston and Mary Kay Lewisville (pharmaceuticals and cosmetics); Nan Ya Plastics Wharton, Berry Global, Advanced Drainage Systems, Diamond Plastics, Charlotte Pipe, Pactiv (plastics); Orion and Cabot (carbon black), TPC Group, Kuraray, Evonik, Nouryon, Solvay/Syensqo, Sasol, Lion Elastomers, Arlanxeo, MEGlobal, Nutrien Borger (chemicals); GAF and Owens Corning (asphalt roofing); Ergon (asphalt terminals, not plants); Continental (no rubber plant in Texas was confirmed); Bridgestone's Firestone Polymers plant at Orange; Goodyear's Bayport plant; Dow's smaller La Porte, Bayport and Beaumont units.
